hypothesis: the ~26s graph build has a reducible cost center; profile-first before changing
assumptions_checked: Respected 90pct mem ceiling (was 87pct) - did NOT run a concurrent 126MB-overlay profiler; read build_route_segments statically instead. Found apply(as.data.frame(df),1,paste) building the cache KEY over ~100k roads, run on EVERY build_route_segments call BEFORE the cache check (line 360) - so paid even on cache hits. Traced callers: per-request path (server.R:415) reuses cached graph and does NOT call it; graph-warm (server.R:834) calls it each data refresh + startup
baseline: apply-paste key build: 1.425s over synthetic 100k x 8 (measured in isolation, memory-safe synthetic - no sf load)
intervention: replaced apply(df,1,paste) with columnwise do.call(paste, c(as.list(df), sep=)) at both key builders (overlay + zip fallback). Cache key => only determinism+collision-resistance needed, not byte-identity; numeric-format change is harmless (one-time cache rebuild)
measurement: isolated benchmark 1.425s -> 0.389s = 3.7x (~1s saved). route.R parses; 2 route_bench runs plan n=8 correctly with new key (cache functional). Within full 23s graph build ~4pct = below build variance; biggest real impact on cache-HIT warms where key-build dominates
effect: MEASURABLE component-level 3.7x reduction (above noise, unlike cycles 17-18 micro-cleanups). End-to-end graph build effect small/below variance; live cache-hit-warm effect ~60pct of that call
conclusion: CONFIRMED real cost-center reduction on a recurring path. Honest: component win clean+measurable; end-to-end route p50 unaffected (build is reused, not per-request). One-time cache rebuild on deploy expected.

hypothesis: an in-house overflow-safe polyline decoder can be byte-identical to the old one on valid input while eliminating the bit-31 NA overflow and getting faster, in both R and Rust(+asm)
assumptions_checked: old R decoder reproducibly warns 'NAs produced by integer overflow' on 7-chunk bit-31 varints (sanity check in gate); valid deltas need <=32 bits so double-space accumulation (exact to 2^53) preserves every value; R rowsum vectorization and Rust i64 kernels divide the same exact integers by 1e5 -> identical IEEE doubles
baseline: R decode_polyline_matrix: per-char substr loop, 32-bit int zigzag (-bitwShiftR(result,1)-1 underflows to NA on malformed input); 2000-pt polyline x20 = 1.481s; no Rust decoder
intervention: R: rewrote decoder (one utf8ToInt pass + rowsum, double-space varints, MAX_CHUNKS=10 malformed guard, truncation semantics preserved). Rust: new flows-core polyline module -- portable kernel + hand-written AArch64 inline-asm varint/zigzag hot loop + flows_polyline_decode C-ABI export for Swift
measurement: tests/test_polyline_decoder.R: 9/9 green (identical() on 500 random valid polylines + extremes + Google spec vector; no warning/NA on overflow input; overlong stops keeping prior pairs; truncation/dangling identical to old). cargo test 26/26 (asm==rust on 2000 corpora + malformed/truncated); clippy 0. R perf: 1.481s -> 0.068s (22x). Smoke test PASS
effect: latent NA-coordinate bug eliminated in both languages; R decode 22x faster; Swift app gains an asm-backed decoder via FFI; all byte-identity contracts hold
conclusion: CONFIRMED -- own decoder is byte-identical on valid input, overflow-safe on malformed input, and strictly faster; asm and portable kernels are equivalence-locked by test
gates: R gate 9/9, cargo 26/26, clippy 0, smoke pass

hypothesis: CH can return the actual shortest PATH (node sequence), not just the cost, by recording each shortcut's bypassed node during contraction and recursively expanding shortcuts at query time -- byte-identical to the locked cost path, unblocking wiring the in-house router into the R production planner (which needs geometry, not just a scalar cost)
assumptions_checked: middle-node bookkeeping can be recorded on EXACTLY the existing !existed shortcut-add condition (the min edge on a pair is always a shortcut iff !existed, so unpacking always resolves the current min edge; originals that stay cheapest keep no middle); recording it never touches the up-graph weights or query loop, so query() stays byte-identical and all cost gates hold; shortcut expansion by explicit stack (right-half then left-half push) emits nodes strictly left-to-right and cannot overflow on deep nesting
baseline: ContractionHierarchy.query returned f64 cost only; no path; CH could rank/select but could not produce route geometry -- the blocker for replacing cppRouting (external C++ dep) with the validated in-house Rust router in R/route_pathfind.R
intervention: rust/flows-core/src/ch.rs: added middle: BTreeMap<(u32,u32),u32> to the struct, populated in contract_node under the same !existed guard as the shortcut count (purely additive, zero change to cost/up-graph construction); new query_path(s,t) -> (f64, Vec<u32>) = same bidirectional upward search as query() plus per-side predecessor + meeting-node tracking, reconstructs the up-graph node sequence s->meet->t, then unpack_edge_into expands every shortcut edge into its two halves iteratively via middle so the result walks only real edges. FFI/R binding deferred to next step
measurement: cargo test 26->28 (2 new: ch_query_path_valid_and_cost_correct = 60 random graphs x10 pairs, ch_query_path_grid_and_edges = 196-node weighted grid all-pairs from 4 sources + s==t); each asserts query_path cost == query() == Dijkstra AND the unpacked path is a real walk s..t whose summed ORIGINAL min-edge weights == Dijkstra (non-circular: Dijkstra is the oracle, path validity checked against the raw CsrGraph edge set). The 5 pre-existing CH cost tests stayed green = cost path byte-identical. clippy 0/all-targets. Release dylib rebuilt (owner 755, passes load guard); R rust_ch_query cost-query still returns 2 on the triangle; runtime smoke PASS
effect: in-house CH now yields full shortest-PATHS provably equal to Dijkstra on cost and valid on geometry, at zero cost-path risk; the last primitive blocking a gated cppRouting replacement in the R planner is in place. Pure-R fallback and all byte-identity contracts untouched
conclusion: CONFIRMED -- shortcut unpacking is correct (path validity + triple cost-equality Dijkstra==query==query_path) and additive (cost tests unchanged), so the CH router can now drive production route geometry. Next: flows_ch_path_c FFI + R binding + a real-WI-graph path-equivalence gate vs the current planner
